title: A Sky Painted From Memory
paragraphs: In the spring of eighteen eighty nine, Vincent van Gogh entered an asylum in the French town of Saint-Remy, seeking relief from his mental illness. He stayed there for about twelve months, and during that year he produced some of his most celebrated work. Among them was The Starry Night, which he painted in mid-June.

The picture was inspired by the view from his window, where he could watch the morning sky just before sunrise. He also wrote to his brother Theo about the morning star he saw from his window. Yet the village below was not copied directly from life. Van Gogh combined what he observed with imagination, memory and emotion. The result is less a record of a place than a picture of a feeling.

Viewers have long noticed the swirling sky, painted in thick, energetic strokes. For many viewers, the sky seems to move, even though the canvas is still. The dark tree in the foreground points upward like a flame, linking the earth to the stars. Today the work belongs to the Museum of Modern Art in New York.
